olivia: Heads-up — I opened a docs PR to migrate the console dashboard JSON schema from v1 -> v2. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1897

olivia: High-level changes: renamed panels.*.viz -> panels.*.type, added layout.grid (rows/cols), removed deprecated `refresh_interval` field. I added a small compat shim in the console renderer but we should update all example files.

kevin: Nice. Is the shim intended to be temporary or long-term?

olivia: Temporary. Goal is to have examples and migration doc updated before the next release so we can drop the shim in 2 weeks.

maria: I can handle updating examples under docs/console/dashboards/examples. Planning to convert three sample dashboards and add a before/after diff. Any preferred style for the diffs?

kevin: Keep diffs minimal. Show only the fields that changed. For the examples repo, add a small script to validate schema against the v2 JSON Schema.

olivia: Added a note in the PR description with the v2 schema link and the validator command. Example validator snippet I used:

```bash
# validate dashboard.json against schema v2
ajv validate -s schemas/dashboard-v2.json -d examples/sample-dashboard-v2.json
```

sachin: Quick correction: the tracing hooks doc links to /sdk/node/observability which returns 404. Should point to /sdk/node/observability/tracing (internal link in the sidebar). I'll push a tiny link-fix commit to the PR unless someone objects.

devex: Please go ahead, sachin. Also we should add a short Node + Python snippet showing how to propagate trace IDs from the app into requests to Redwood so Console traces can join. Suggested Node snippet:

```js
// attach trace header when calling Redwood API
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const traceId = getCurrentTraceId(); // from your tracing lib
await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`, 'X-Trace-Id': traceId },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt })
});
```

and Python: 

```py
# requests example
import requests
trace_id = tracer.current_span().context.trace_id
headers = { 'Authorization': f'Bearer {API_KEY}', 'X-Trace-Id': str(trace_id) }
requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', headers=headers, json={ 'prompt': prompt })
```

maria: I'll add those to the tracing hooks page and include a short note about how Console maps X-Trace-Id -> trace_link in the UI.

olivia: Also added a new doc under console/observability/costs.md with a worked example showing cost vs latency tradeoffs for sync vs streaming routes. Reviewers: please sanity-check the numbers (I used sample throughput 50 rps, 1.2 tokens/ms latency).

kevin: I skimmed — numbers look fine but add a caveat about model quantization impacting token/ms estimates.

olivia: Good call, added a caveat and link to the Optimize quantization guide.

docs-bot: Mentioning @maria @sachin for review — PR 1897 needs 2 approvals.

maria: Reviewing now, should finish by EOD.

sachin: Link-fix pushed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/commit/2b7a1c4 (small change to sidebar nav).

deploy-bot: docs CI passed — 12 files changed, 3 added. :white_check_mark:

olivia: Awesome, thanks everyone. After approvals I'll merge and coordinate a short note for the weekly docs sync.

kevin: If anyone wants to test the validator locally ping me and I'll share a Docker container with ajv + node.

maria: Will do — thanks! :thumbsup:
